claim: Telling a person or model to be less biased, or to reflect, rarely removes bias; effort-based fixes (money, accountability, awareness) work only when the bias comes from low effort.
schema_part: G guardrails; 4b not-to-add: generic reminder checklists
agent_test: Add a 'be aware of bias X' line vs none at equal tokens on anchoring and framing items; expect near-zero change.

claim: Rule training (statistical principles, normative rules) transfers only where the bias is a missing-rule error; biases that are inhibition or intuition errors do not improve, and transfer fades over weeks.
schema_part: O rule library as operator input; memory
agent_test: Put base-rate and sample-size rules into the scaffold and test on rule-type vs intuition-type bias items.

claim: One-shot game training with personalised feedback cut human bias more than a video and persisted 2-3 months (game -46.25% and -31.94% immediately, -34.76% and -23.57% at follow-up; video -18.60% and -25.70% then -20.10% and -19.20%, Exp 1 and Exp 2; numbers verified in body text, the abstract quotes a different mix). An independent team (Martey et al. 2014, different game, 8-week follow-up) also found the game beat a video: combined bias score 19.91 to 2.44 vs video 18.65 to 14.82 at post-test, game advantage on FAE and CB, none on bias blind spot; the effect decays by 8 weeks and retention N is small (30-40 per cell).
agent_test: LLM analogue: store feedback on past errors in memory; compare with no memory at equal tokens. Two teams now agree on the immediate effect; nothing beyond 8-12 weeks.

claim: Debiasing training can transfer to an unannounced real-style case: 58.8% vs 72.2% chose the confirming race option, odds ratio 0.549 (verified), N=290; the effect did not fade between 1 and 52 days.
agent_test: Test a forced disconfirming-evidence step on Challenger-style cases.

claim: The training effect on confirmation bias runs through more disconfirming arguments, not through lower confidence (confidence beta .16, p=.053).
agent_test: Ablate the disconfirm step against a confidence-calibration step.

claim: A conceptual replication in 71 national risk analysts and 118 students found the one-shot training cut confirmation bias in experts too (F(1,169)=20.74, eta2=.109), with no group-by-intervention interaction; the bias blind spot persisted and did not predict real bias.
agent_test: Same lab lineage as the original; counts as replication in a new population, not a fully independent group.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Prospective hindsight and consider-the-opposite are recommended but have little field effect-size evidence, and consider-the-opposite can backfire when listing many alternatives feels hard.
agent_test: Pre-mortem vs consider-opposite vs none at equal tokens; measure accuracy and over-correction.

claim: A cognitive forcing checklist did not reduce diagnostic error in a randomised vignette study (2.8 vs 3.1 cases correct, 95% CI -0.94 to 0.45, p=.49; verified) but checklists are said to help forgetting errors in procedural tasks.
agent_test: Checklist scaffold vs none, split by forgetting-type vs judgement-type tasks. Study kept 76 of 320 respondents.

claim: Changing the question format beats changing the person: SPIES bins removed overprecision at 90% (hit rate 88.35% vs 73.79%); asking for 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles raises hit rate about 20 points.
schema_part: O elicitation operator: distribution before point
agent_test: Ask the agent for bin probabilities vs a single interval on forecast items; compare calibration at equal tokens. LLM side: asking for a 90% interval does not calibrate GPT-3.5/4o-mini (hit-average 18-68% against 60-95% nominal; d10); SPIES itself is untested on LLMs.

claim: Averaging two estimates from the same person gives about half the gain of averaging two people; a delay helps.
agent_test: Sample twice with different prompts and average; compare with independent models.

claim: Short probabilistic-reasoning training improved real forecasts in a randomised tournament (743 forecasters, 199 questions; training r=.17, teaming r=.30; verified). Multiple R is .43 with dispositions plus situation and .64 once behaviour is added (belief updating beta .45); the two figures in the evidence file are different nested models, not a conflict.
schema_part: S update state; G outside view
agent_test: Outside-view, averaging and bias-warning module vs none on forecasting questions.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLMs show human-like biases (anchoring, framing, primacy, group attribution) across many models; all 30 tested biases appear in some of 20 models, and bias-consistent answers occur in 17.8-57.3% of instances across 45 models.
agent_test: Run a bias battery on our agent before and after the scaffold.

claim: Instruction tuning and RLHF raise some biases (decoy, certainty, belief) relative to base models.
agent_test: Compare base vs tuned model under the same scaffold.

claim: Generic prompt debiasing (awareness, ignore-the-hint, CoT, principles, reflection) does not reliably remove LLM anchoring; the best gain is about 10 points (Llama-3.1-8B 34.7% to 24.7% with Anti-DP, verified), and none in Lou and Sun.
schema_part: 4b: do not add a generic reflect prompt
agent_test: Add a reflect or ignore instruction at equal tokens; expect a small effect.

claim: Reasoning models are less anchored: total anchored ratio GPT-4o 27.3%, DeepSeek-R1 25.0%, Qwen3-235B thinking 22.0% vs Mistral-7B 51.1% and Qwen2.5-0.5B 60.5% (verified for 0.5B, GPT-4o, R1, Qwen3). Counter-evidence: in a matched-sibling dose-response test (Kraishan 2026, 7 models, 12,350 calls) reasoning models were not less biased (Delta=+0.031, p=.157) and more realised thinking did not lower bias; the two studies measure different things (anchored ratio vs signed score on 5 items per bias).
agent_test: Compare thinking on and off at matched token budgets; more tokens are not equal tokens.

claim: Changing the input (neutral restatement, both low and high anchors, extra distractor options) works more often than adding instructions.
agent_test: Rewrite the prompt neutrally then answer, vs instruct; similar token cost.

claim: Self-help rewriting works for strong models (GPT-4 framing gap -0.405 to -0.010) but weak models change too many decisions or collapse (Llama-2 7B contrastive admit 0.996, reject 1.000).
schema_part: O reframe operator gated on capability
agent_test: Test the rewrite operator on a strong and a small model.

claim: An iterative detect-analyse-rewrite loop (SACD) beat CoT, self-help, few-shot and debate on three domains: FOMC llama3.1-8b 0.1570 vs vanilla 0.3805 (verified); removing the analysis step hurts most.
agent_test: Reproduce at equal tokens against best-of-N; token cost was not equalised in the source.

claim: Multi-agent debate and Reflexion can raise bias (FOMC debate 0.5020 vs vanilla 0.3805, verified); same-model debate entrenches shared errors.
agent_test: Same-model debate vs single pass vs diverse-perspective debate at equal tokens.

claim: Prompt-level debiasing is uneven by bias family: Response biases improve (+40.5%), Judgment worsens (-4.4%), Information Processing is flat (-1.1%).
agent_test: Test per-family routing vs one generic debias prompt.

claim: Representation-level steering cuts LLM bias 26-32% but with a capability cost that varies by model.
agent_test: Not testable in a prompt-only scaffold.

claim: More detailed prompts reduce most biases (up to 14.9%) but one bias (Overattribution) got worse; size above 32B helped in 39.5% of cases.
agent_test: Detail ladder at fixed tokens.

claim: A role-based multi-agent clinical review with a devil's advocate gave top-2 differential accuracy 76% (61/80) while the initial diagnosis was correct 0/80.
agent_test: Single-agent devil's-advocate pass vs multi-agent at equal tokens.

claim: LLM bias measures are sensitive to wording and repeat variance, so single-prompt results are fragile.
agent_test: Use paraphrase sets and 10 or more repeats for every test.

claim: Supplying or eliciting the missing rule before the decision cut LLM bias sensitivity about 51% on average (12.9% to about 6.3% at best; p<.001) where CoT (16.1%) and self-debias wording (8.3%, not significant per bias) did not. This is the first LLM support for the missing-rule vs reminder split.
schema_part: O rule-elicitation operator before decide state; G1-G12 vs 4b generic reminders
agent_test: Rule-elicit step vs CoT vs none at equal tokens on 100+ matched biased/unbiased pairs per bias; split items by missing-rule vs intuition type.

claim: Extra thinking budget does not lower judgement bias: across 4 model families no slope of bias on realised reasoning tokens was significantly negative (range 0-3,440 tokens), and requested ceilings were often not realised (GPT-5.1 used 116-118 tokens at any ceiling).
schema_part: S extended-reasoning state; do not add reasoning budget as a debiaser
agent_test: Fixed-cost comparison: thinking on at 1k vs 4k tokens vs a one-line input restatement, with realised tokens logged.

claim: A prompt-level pre-mortem or 'could you be wrong?' step has no measured debiasing effect on LLM decisions; the only items are a demonstration (Hills 2025) and a harm-listing safety method (InvThink: up to 32% less harmful output).
agent_test: Pre-answer failure listing vs post-answer 'could you be wrong' vs none at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs are overprecise on numeric interval questions and do not widen intervals when asked for higher confidence; CoT helped GPT-4o-mini (MMLU hit rate 68.04% to 80.49%) but not GPT-3.5, and self-refinement mostly hurt.
schema_part: O elicitation operator: distribution before point
agent_test: Compare single interval, SPIES bins and 10/50/90 fractiles on forecast items for hit rate and width.

claim: Carrying forward the agent's own earlier interpretations can create anchoring: in long ICU trajectories removing insight memory raised Hit@5 from 0.526 to 0.601 (Qwen3-235B); structured memory improved results but left unsafe recommendations.
schema_part: memory: store errors and corrections, not conclusions
agent_test: Memory of past errors with corrections vs memory of past conclusions vs none.

claim: Same-model multi-agent debate raised judge bias after round 1 and kept it raised; one debiased critic gave small gains (position consistency 0.817 to 0.831 over 3 rounds, GPT-4o-mini judge).
agent_test: Equal-token debate vs single debiased pass; role-diverse vs same-model agents.

claim: LLM debiasing tests with few items cannot detect typical gains: Kraishan used 5 items per bias (anchor-restate effect p=.057 with 5 of 5 items in the helpful direction) and PROBE-SWE open-ended arms used 40 items with CIs about 35 points wide; use 100+ items, paraphrases and 10+ repeats, analysed per item.
agent_test: Power plan before any debiasing arm is run.
